ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory positive identification and risk-based enhanced due diligence for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined under Article (9) of Law No. 80/2002 and the Executive Regulations; screening of all shareholders, directors, managers, and UBGs against United Nations consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, United Kingdom OFSI consolidated list, Egypt's own terrorist entities list maintained by the National Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (AMLU/EG), and the Arab League sanctions list. Systemically repeated screening at onboarding and on an ongoing basis (at least every 30 days or upon any change in ownership structure). Failure to screen or to report a match results in administrative penalty and criminal liability under the AML law.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Investor Electronic Portal and the Commercial Registry Online System (trade registry name clearance through the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones 'GAFI' at https://www.gafi.gov.eg and the Ministry of Interior's Commercial Registration Department)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Every company name must be registered and published in Arabic. For foreign-invested or foreign-brand entities, the Arabic name is the primary legal name, and the Latin transliteration is filed for auxiliary identification only. The Arabic name must comply with standard Arabic spelling and phonetic transliteration of non-Arabic proper nouns. Two-step name clearance is required: first, a name reservation certificate in Arabic from GAFI; second, the same name must be approved for commercial registry. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any prior registered name in the same classification of activities or public domain.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: ANY WORD THAT INCITES RELIGIOUS OR SECTARIAN CONFLICT
ANY EXPRESSION CONTRARY TO PUBLIC ORDER OR MORALITY
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the incorporation attorney must file a written administrative appeal with the GAFI Legal Affairs and Appeals Committee within 15 calendar days of the written rejection notice. The appeal must annex the proposed alternative name, a certified copy of the rejection notice, and a memorandum on the distinguishability of the rejected name from any protected name. The appeal is decided within 10 working days. If the appeal is granted, a fresh name reservation certificate is issued for the original validity window. If rejected, the applicant may file a fresh name application with a new proposed name or seek judicial review before the Administrative Court (Egyptian Council of State) within 60 days of the final administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a fabless semiconductor design firm under ISIC 2610, a pure virtual office is generally not permissible as the registered office must be a physically accessible location capable of receiving official notifications, maintaining statutory books, and accommodating periodic inspection by GAFI, the tax authority, and the Commercial Registry. However, a shared service or serviced office space with a dedicated suite and address (including certain GAFI-licensed business centers) may satisfy the statutory mandate. A telecommunication-only virtual address without a physical desk or storage is not accepted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections is moderate-to-high at 45% during the first two years of operation, especially because the company is registered under a licensing-required activity (semiconductor design) and uses the standard LLC form. GAFI and the Taxation Authority conduct initial post-incorporation inspections of at least 30% of newly registered entities in the technology sector on an unannounced basis within 12 months. Factual presence of a staffed office, tangible equipment, and corporate records will materially reduce follow-up inspections.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018, particularly Articles 1, 3, 5, 26–53 (Limited Liability Companies); Executive Regulations issued by Ministry of Investment Resolution No. 96 of 1982; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 for investor facilities and incentives; Commercial Registration Law No. 34 of 1976.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Department via the One-Stop-Shop window; final registration and trade-name archiving through the Commercial Registry, Ministry of Trade and Industry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association of the Limited Liability Company (Shoirkat Khassat Al-Masouliyat Al-Mahdoodah), notarized in Arabic by an Egyptian notary public.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No fixed statutory minimum capital is prescribed for an LLC under Companies Law No. 159/1981; the authorized capital and the subscribed, allotted shares are stated in the Memorandum of Association. All shares must be fully subscribed; no escrow deposit is mandatory, but the subscription funds or in-kind contribution documentation must be evidenced at registration and confirmed in the first board resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the founders, having subscribed to the entire authorized capital of the Limited Liability Company under Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, do hereby approve and adopt the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association. The registered office shall be situated at [address in Egypt] where the legal administration and corporate books will be kept. The issued shares are allocated to the subscribing partners as recorded in the incorporation minutes. [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer and [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, each with authority to sign, open bank accounts, and execute contracts. The officers are directed to complete GAFI, tax, social insurance, and licensing filings immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Pre-incorporation Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Name Reservation Portal and the Commercial Registry trade-name screening unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online name reservation application with GAFI; submit Arabic and transliterated trade names in order of preference; obtain an official name approval certificate showing the name is not identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered mark or company. Secure a legal Egyptian registered office address and prepare a lease or ownership document for the intended head office.
required_dossiers: Passport copy or national ID of each founding partner
Notarized power of attorney if a founder is represented by another person
Three proposed company names in Arabic with the trade-name suffix 'LLC'
Proposed legal address / office letter of intent or lease draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, a formal written retraction of the conflicting name must be filed by the prior registrant or the applicant must submit two new alternative names through the GAFI portal; resubmission is free of charge and is processed within two business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office within the Ministry of Justice district where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Arabic Memorandum and Articles of Association in conformity with the LLC standard template of GAFI. All founders or their legal representatives must appear before the notary public to sign, and signatures must be authenticated. The document must specify the LLC name, object (including fabless integrated-circuit design and IP licensing), capital, share allocations, management structure, and registered office. The notary assigns a notarization number and date to the executed instrument.
required_dossiers: GAFI name approval certificate
Passport or national ID of each founder
Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic, prepared by an Egyptian licensed attorney
Original power of attorney if a founder is represented
Valid national ID or passport of each legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies drafting defects or missing statements, the document is corrected and re-signed the same day; if a founder is absent, a supplemental notarized power of attorney must be supplied; re-attestation is completed within not more than two additional business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing with GAFI and Commercial Registry Entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop-Shop, Companies Registration Department; Commercial Registry under the Ministry of Trade and Industry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association, name certificate, and registered-office lease to the GAFI One-Stop-Shop. Pay the statutory registration, stamp, publication, and commercial register fees. GAFI verifies compliance, approves the company formation, and issues the incorporation certificate. GAFI then forwards the extraction to the Commercial Registry for the registry number and commercial register entry, and the Official Publication is made in the Official Gazette.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation application form A1
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
GAFI name reservation certificate
Valid passport or national ID copies of all founding partners
Notarized office lease agreement or proof of ownership of the registered office
Founder minutes/board resolution appointing the first directors and authorizing signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI raises a compliance query, an additional response memorandum with corrected or supplemental documentation and a statement of compliance must be submitted within ten working days; refusal may be appealed in writing to the GAFI Internal Complaints Committee, with statutory processing within thirty business days. Any missing commercial-registry data is cured via an amended-notice submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Social Insurance, and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA); National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI); Commercial Bank of the company's choice in Egypt
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the post-incorporation tax registration with the ETA to obtain the corporate Tax Identification Number and corporate tax card. Register for VAT in accordance with the mandatory VAT registration threshold or voluntary registration for the intended invoice / supply chain. Open a corporate bank account for Egyptian Pounds and foreign currency; deposit any cash portion of the paid-up capital and obtain a bank certificate. Register all founding shareholder-employees and any subsequently employed personnel with the National Organization for Social Insurance within 14 days of commencement of work.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation issued by GAFI
Commercial registry extract
Tax ID form and corporate tax registration form
Bank deposit certificate or proof of paid-in capital
Office lease contract and proof of address
List of directors, officers, and employees for NOSI registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA queries the registration, the company must respond with a corrected tax form and the missing certificates; a temporary tax ID and fast-track registration may be obtained from the ETA central service center. NOSI disputes are resolved by submitting employment contracts and the commercial registry extract to the Social Insurance Authority; late fees may be waived for good-cause delay, otherwise an appeal is submitted within thirty days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Environmental, and Civil Defense Pre-clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Industrial Development Authority; Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency; Civil Defense Authority of the Ministry of Interior
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit to the Industrial Development Authority an activity classification statement confirming that the company performs fabless integrated-circuit design, EDA software, and IP licensing as a non-manufacturing or R&D-service activity, thereby qualifying for a service/industrial record rather than a factory license. If a cleanroom or laboratory is established, submit the environmental screening questionnaire through the Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency online portal and obtain the appropriate environmental category. Complete a workplace safety and fire-safety inspection with the Civil Defense Authority and secure the occupancy/premises safety certificate.
required_dossiers: Incorporation certificate and commercial registry extract
IDA automated licensing activity form and classification request
Detailed business scope description for ISIC 2610 fabless design
Office or R&D lab lease and floor plans
EEAA Environmental Form B questionnaire and supporting emissions/data sheets where applicable
Civil Defense fire-safety application and premises inspection sheet
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IDA refers the activity for an industrial manufacturing license because the classification is contested, the company may submit a formal classification appeal with reference to ISIC 2610 design, NAICS 334413 fabless, and business-model evidence showing no physical wafer fabrication. If the EEAA questions the Form B screening, an additional scoping study or binding mitigation plan is submitted within the statutory response window; Civil Defense corrective notice items must be rectified before re-inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA), Egyptian Ministry of Trade and Industry
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Activity Record and Service Enterprise License for Fabless Semiconductor Design and IP Licensing under Industrial Licensing Law No. 15 of 2017 and Law No. 159 of 1981

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency - Central Administration for Environmental Impact Assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - environmental scoping/registration; purely office-based fabless design activity may qualify for a Form B screening registration, while installation of limited R&D laboratory or cleanroom requires a restricted scoping study and mitigation commitments under Executive Regulations of Law No. 4 of 1994
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No regulated point-source industrial wastewater or solvent emissions may be discharged without treatment; R&D laboratory effluent, if any, must meet the discharge limits of Ministerial Decree No. 44 of 2000 for sewer water, including pH 6.5-9.0 and maximum residue requirements; hazardous chemical waste, acid/alkaline etchants, dopants, and solvent waste must be segregated and handled or removed by an officially licensed waste transporter; e-waste must comply with Waste Management Regulation Law No. 202 of 2020

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Authority fire-safety certificate for all occupied premises, including certified fire extinguishers, emergency exits, smoke alarms, and electrical load compliance; Labor Office workplace-safety clearance under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003 covering interior ventilation, electricity permits, workstation ergonomics, and occupational risk assessment

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance, Cairo; official e-portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing and e-receipts platform: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg with API-based transaction clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: After commercial registration with GAFI/Egyptian Commercial Registry, the foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must apply for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) and statutory VAT ID via the ETA online tax card system within 30 days of commencing activities. The e-application requires: certified copy of the Memorandum of Association, Commercial Registration Certificate, board resolution appointing the tax representative, proof of Egyptian registered office, valid director identification, and bank confirmation of capital contribution. Upon issuance, the TIN/VAT ID is automatically activated for e-invoicing after obtaining a qualified digital signature certificate; VAT registration is filed separately on the same ETA portal upon crossing the statutory registration threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch pass-through election exists in Egypt. An Egyptian LLC is mandatorily a separate taxable resident entity taxed on worldwide income at the corporate rate (22.5% top rate, lower brackets for small business under the simplified regime). Elections available are limited to: (i) the simplified tax regime for qualifying micro/small entities under ETA thresholds; (ii) tax treaty relief through an Egyptian tax residence certificate; (iii) licensing as a free-zone company under GAFI with special VAT/customs treatment; and (iv) selection of accounting method for VAT input deduction, subject to ETA approval.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover for goods; EGP 250,000 annual taxable turnover for services; compulsory registration applies once cumulative supply exceeds the relevant threshold; voluntary registration is allowed below the threshold at ETA discretion.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt operates a mandatory real-time e-invoicing/e-receipt clearance regime in phased roll-out for all ETA-registered taxpayers. Every invoice issued by the LLC must be transmitted through an ETA-approved ERP/API integration to the ETA central clearance system, validated within seconds, and digitally stamped with a Unique UUID and QR code. The invoice file must include Arabic content and amounts in EGP; rejected or missing invoices are treated as unlawful and deny the buyer's input VAT deduction. B2B sales, export invoices, and credit/debit notes are all subject to the same fiscal clearance and 5-year archival mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical export of semiconductor goods and cross-border fabless services/IP licensing supplied to foreign customers is zero-rated under Article 17 of the VAT Law No. 67 of 2016, provided: (i) tangible goods physically leave Egypt and are declared to customs; (ii) design, R&D, and IP-licensing services are supplied to a non-resident customer with economic use wholly outside Egypt; (iii) consideration is paid in foreign currency and remitted to an Egyptian bank account; (iv) documentary evidence is retained with the ETA; and export proceeds repatriation occurs within the statutory period.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (official customs single-window export declaration stating HS code 8542 or relevant semiconductor classification)
Commercial Invoice and Export/Licensing Contract with the foreign buyer
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical exit from Egypt
Inward Remittance Certificate or CBE bank confirmation of foreign-currency repatriation
ETA zero-rated e-invoice batch report bearing the digital QR/UUID stamp
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA applies a targeted audit ledger for all zero-rated and refunded exports, cross-checking the customs exit record, logistics movement, e-invoice clearance, and Central Bank of Egypt FX remittance statements. Any false, incomplete, or tardy zero-rating claim triggers full clawback of the VAT refund, statutory interest from the original refund date, an administrative fine of up to 100% of the evaded tax, and, in cases of proved fraud or falsified documentation, criminal penalties including imprisonment of up to 5 years and debarment from the export refund fast-track.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), operating under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 88 of 2003 as consolidated and extensively amended by Law No. 194 of 2020; the CBE is the sole foreign-exchange licensing and monetary authority, while the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) approves FDI registrations under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and the Egyptian Tax Authority enforces fiscal clearances precedent to cross-border remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a managed-flexible, market-determined exchange-rate regime following the March 2024 unified float supported by the IMF Extended Fund Facility. Current-account payments for trade, services, IP royalties, and profit repatriation are legally transferable against adequate documentation. Capital-account transactions such as equity injections, shareholder loans, and portfolio flows remain subject to CBE registration, bank-level approval, and practical sensitivity to dollar-liquidity cycles. Profit remittance is legally guaranteed under Article 13 of Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 but in bank practice requires audited financial statements, board-approved dividend distribution, settlement of the 10% non-resident dividend withholding tax, and ETA tax-clearance certification; post-float, documentary-complete remittances are converted and cleared at the unified market rate, although invisible rationing can emerge during severe FX stress.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: CBE Circular 117 of 2022, as tightened during 2023, had imposed a mandatory surrender ratio on export proceeds rising from 50% to 100% together with a repatriation window aligned to the standard 180-day term. Following the March 6, 2024 foreign-exchange liberalization, the mandatory conversion-to-bank ratio has been suspended effectively to zero; exporters must nonetheless repatriate the full export invoice value through the collecting Egyptian bank within the statutory 180 days calculated from the bill-of-lading or air-waybill date. The underlying trade contracts, ACI/ACID customs declarations, shipping documents, and SWIFT MT103 advices must be retained for the 5-year bank record-keeping period, and non-compliance exposes the exporter to CBE penalty lists and cancellation of bank credit facilities.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (USD) and Operational Current Account (EGP/USD)
Operational Current Account (EGP/USD) with parallel Foreign-Currency Account
Operational Current Account (EGP/USD), Trade Finance and Documentary Credit Line
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Current Account
Multi-Currency Corporate Account (EGP, USD, EUR) with global-liquidity sweep capability
Operational Current Account (EGP/USD) and Import LC Lines

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: LOW-MEDIUM as a supplement only: offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut Business, Payoneer, and Airwallex hold no CBE license, cannot open EGP accounts, cannot issue Egyptian IBANs, and cannot serve as the primary collection account for Egyptian-domiciled receivables. Using them as the principal treasury channel breaches CBE repatriation obligations and the documentary-evidence rule for IP-royalty inflows. They are defensible solely as auxiliary payout rails for foreign foundry subcontractors and global contractor payments, provided the Egyptian operating account at a licensed bank remains the account of record for Egyptian revenue and every EMI drawdown is mirrored by a corresponding SWIFT credit into Egypt within the statutory repatriation period.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory: Egyptian banks require the general manager and all ultimate beneficial owners to attend an in-branch account-opening and AML risk-rating interview; fully remote or video-KYC opening is not accepted by CBE-supervised banks for a newly formed LLC with non-resident ownership. Foreign UBOs may deputize a resident signatory under a notarized, apostilled, or consular-legalized power of attorney, but the UBO must nevertheless appear personally on at least one occasion for biometric capture and source-of-wealth interview. Corporate documents drafted in English must be tendered with certified Arabic translation, and the bank's board-resolution forms and signature-card specimens must be physically executed before bank officers during the first visit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO ownership of an intangible-asset firm with no physical factory or warehouse in Egypt
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: English/Arabic authenticated constitutional documents and register of beneficial owners; GAFI LLC incorporation certificate and unified tax card; local office lease and payroll evidence; engineering-team employment contracts; sources-of-wealth statements from foreign UBOs; bank reference letters from foreign parent banks; signed compliance declaration describing the fabless revenue model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border IP-royalty inflows flagged for round-tripping or transfer-mispricing screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed license and design-service contracts with end-client names and fee schedules; OECD-aligned transfer-pricing summary demonstrating arm's-length royalty rates; VAT e-invoices submitted to the ETA e-invoicing system; audited annual financial statements and cash-flow projections; Beneficial-Owner and Transaction-Purpose Letter confirming the license is exercised by Egyptian residents where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large, asymmetric first-year capital injection from an offshore shareholders' account routed via an intermediary bank
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholders' resolution and amended articles of association increasing equity; GAFI electronic-license and FDI registration confirmation; source-of-funds ledger showing the full chain of bank transfers to the shareholder account with no crypto legs; bank-to-bank reference; signed undertaking that funds will be applied to payroll, R&D tools, and subcontract deposits within Egypt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent outbound disbursements for wafer/foundry subcontracting and design-tool licenses that resemble profit-stripping
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foundry purchase orders and proforma invoices; corresponding documentary credits (MT700) or telegraphic-transfer instructions; evidence of economic activity in the form of IC design milestones, schematics, and mask-set documentation; corporate tax filings and withholding-tax certificates proving Egyptian tax paid on margins; intra-group service agreements supported by transfer-pricing documentation aligned to OECD Chapters I-VI.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Any hit on sanctions or PEP screening, or attempted settlement via crypto-asset intermediaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening performed on all shareholders, directors, and counterparties; standing board policy prohibition on crypto settlement; bank statements of the sole designated corporate account; legal opinion that no digital-asset payment rail will be used; management remediation letter with an audit trail to compliance for any one-off historic contact.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The parent or shareholder executes a SWIFT MT103 wire to the Egyptian LLC's Capital Escrow FDI sub-account inside a licensed bank using the BPM6 purpose description 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital Injection (Increase of Capital)'. The bank files the CBE FDI registration on the company's behalf, and the credit is posted as restricted capital until the GAFI certificate of capital contribution is uploaded. The verification bundle comprises board minutes on the capital increase, updated articles of association registered with GAFI, the bank's FDI registration form, a funds-application commitment letter, and, where software tools or intangibles are contributed in-kind, a certified valuation report.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For imports of wafer fabrication and design-tool services the compliant rails are: (i) a commercial documentary credit issued under SWIFT MT700 from the Egyptian bank to the foundry's bank; or (ii) following the December 2023 liberalization, direct telegraphic transfer under SWIFT MT103 upon verified FX availability and bank credit and source-of-funds approval. For IP-license and royalty payments abroad, SWIFT MT103 is used under the current-account category designated BPM6 'Charges for the Use of Intellectual Property', accompanied by the signed license agreement, ETA withholding-tax receipt, and VAT e-invoice; letters of credit are not used for owned IP royalties because the underlying is non-goods-related, although they may be used defensively for prepaid tool subscriptions when the beneficiary requires bank-payment risk mitigation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EGP/USD Forwards with final physical settlement at maturity (tenor 1-12 months, available against documented underlying trade or invoice exposure and a bank credit facility)
Onshore FX Swaps and value-date swaps executed at the unified market rate
Cross-Currency Swaps (EGP/USD) subject to CBE prior approval and documented matching cash-flow exposure
Plain-vanilla USD put / EGP call options offered by licensed banks for covered corporate hedging

Offshore NDFs: NOT permissible as onshore Egyptian corporate hedging; any non-deliverable arrangement booked offshore would contravene CBE supervision and is excluded from the compliant treasury blueprint

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Tax Form 41) with audited financial statements and transfer pricing declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) via the e-Tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year LLC, by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine up to EGP 20,000 plus monthly late-payment penalty of 2% of unpaid tax; prolonged default triggers enforced collection, bank garnishment, suspension of tax clearance certificate, and commercial registry restrictions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited annual financial statements and General Assembly approval record filed with GAFI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) and the competent Commercial Registry office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements prepared within 3 months of fiscal year-end; General Assembly convened within 6 months; GAFI filing by 30 June for calendar-year entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EGP 10,000 to EGP 100,000 under Companies Law 159 of 1981; repeated default can lead to GAFI administrative suspension and forced dissolution proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry regularization (Izhar) and Chamber of Commerce subscription
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry under the Ministry of Trade and Industry; local Chamber of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of registration update and annual Chamber subscription due by the end of May each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine EGP 500 to EGP 5,000; continued default results in suspension of the commercial registration certificate (Izhar) and blockage of license renewals and bank account operations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) register annual confirmation and change notification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) procedures via the company's AML compliance officer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual sign-off at the time of financial statements approval; any UBO change filed within 15 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Imprisonment and fine of EGP 100,000 to EGP 500,000 under AML Law 80 of 2002; EMLCU may prohibit directors from holding positions in regulated entities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual payroll and social insurance reconciliation declaration (Form 2 annual settlement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly Form 1/2 filings by the 15th of the following month; annual reconciliation statement within 30 days of fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears penalty of 1% per day of unpaid contributions; company managers and directors jointly liable; NOSI may impose an additional 50% surcharge and enforce against bank accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Transfer pricing disclosure form (Form C-1) with annual TP documentation for related-party IP licensing transactions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Transfer Pricing Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the Corporate Income Tax Return within 4 months of fiscal year-end; TP documentation file prepared before filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with Egyptian Transfer Pricing Guidelines results in fines up to EGP 1,000,000 and deemed-royalty adjustments at 22.5% corporate tax plus 2% monthly interest

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for every Egyptian LLC regardless of size under Companies Law 159 of 1981; audited financial statements must accompany the corporate tax return and be filed with GAFI. Medium and large taxpayers with revenue above EGP 50 million are additionally required to maintain e-invoice/e-receipt audit trails and extended tax audit data readiness.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which are equivalent to IFRS with national interpretations; listed/unlisted entities with securities offerings apply full IFRS. Fabless semiconductor IP licensing revenue is recognized in accordance with EAS 32 Revenue and Service Contracts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The shareholders/partners and UBO information must be reconfirmed annually at the General Assembly and by the external auditor; shareholding transfers above USD 5,000 or 5% of capital must be registered in the share transfer register and reported to the EMLCU within 15 days. Final confirmation is filed with the annual financial statements at GAFI.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Transfers (Register of Capital Transfers)
Register of Mortgages and Charges on Assets
Minute Book of General Assembly Meetings
Minute Book of Board of Managers Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - 1,200 per year for a serviced registered office in Cairo or Giza; local tax/administrative representative retainer USD 500 - 2,000 per year
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - 6,000 per year for a fabless semiconductor entity with international IP licensing and limited local operational footprint

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax holidays and preferential rates for qualifying investments in technology, manufacturing, and free zone enterprises; reduced rates for certain export-oriented activities

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 100 or equivalent) via the Egyptian Tax Authority e-Filing Portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss calculation including adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents, include attribution of profits to permanent establishment and adjust for treaty provisions
Claim credits for taxes withheld on cross-border payments

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Penalties of 1% of the tax due per month of delay, up to a maximum of 10% of the tax due, plus interest at the Central Bank rate on unpaid amounts

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Egyptian Tax Authority, submit to the paying entity or bank, and apply for reduced withholding tax rate under the applicable Double Tax Agreement (DTA)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 15% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% under DTAs; Interest: 15% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% under DTAs

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 500,000,000 (approximately USD 10 million) for local file requirements
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Mandatory Economic Substance Regulations apply to companies engaged in IP holding, distribution, or certain service activities; requires adequate physical presence, core income-generating activities, and substance in Egypt

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income, false invoicing, or failure to remit withheld taxes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution with fines up to 3 times the evaded tax amount, imprisonment for up to 5 years, and confiscation of assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability, including imprisonment and disqualification from office

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a company without adequate economic substance for its activities, particularly in IP or holding structures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties, dissolution of the company, and back taxation with interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines and potential imprisonment for responsible officers

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or maintain TP documentation or apply arm's length principle in related party transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to EGP 1 million or 10% of revenue, plus adjustments to taxable income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for fines and potential criminal charges if willful
